pages.lesson:
LESSON: LISTENING FOR GIST: ATTENTIVE LISTENING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.2: Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can you show love to your family members?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify vocabulary on nuclear family members from an oral text for information
2. appreciate attentive listening in communication for lifelong learning

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: LISTENING FOR GIST: ATTENTIVE LISTENING
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening helps you succeed in ARABIC LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: LISTENING FOR GIST: ATTENTIVE LISTENING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify vocabulary on nuclear family members from an oral text for information

What this means
In this part you learn to identify vocabulary on nuclear family members from an oral text for information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify vocabulary on nuclear family members from an oral text for information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify vocabulary on nuclear family members from an oral text for information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate attentive listening in communication for lifelong learning

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate attentive listening in communication for lifelong learning. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate attentive listening in communication for lifelong learning.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate attentive listening in communication for lifelong learning. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify vocabulary on nuclear family members from an oral text for information)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening to a partner. (skill: appreciate attentive listening in communication for lifelong learning)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify vocabulary on nuclear family members from an oral text for information.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate attentive listening in communication for lifelong learning.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can you show love to your family members?
2. How can we listen to texts attentively?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify vocabulary on nuclear family members from an oral text for information.
5. Be able to: appreciate attentive listening in communication for lifelong learning.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
